subject: Dedicated capacity and burst policy — NorthStar Labs (operational SLA outline)
messages:
From: Maya Johnson <maya.johnson@northstarlabs.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudOps <cloudops@northstarlabs.com>, Procurement <procurement@northstarlabs.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: NorthStar launch — Dedicated capacity sizing 

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are finalizing capacity numbers for an internal product launch (target date: 2026-01-12) and want to lock in a Dedicated plan that can absorb a predictable launch spike. High level:  -- expected steady-state model traffic ~120 rps across our critical endpoints;  -- expected peak (first 72 hours after launch): 4x steady-state for sustained 6–12 hour windows;  -- occasional microbursts up to 8x for short intervals (~10–30 minutes).

Primary asks: can Redwood commit to a controlled burst policy for a reserved pool (we'd like runbook + SLOs), and what are the guardrails for autoscaling (prewarm times, eviction, fallback to smaller models)? Also want to understand how credits or short-term burst capacity would be accounted against committed spend. Procurement asked us to get an operational SLA outline and a mutual action plan to attach to the SOW.

Can you send a recommended sizing and an ops-level policy we can review with CloudOps and Procurement?

Thanks,
Maya Johnson
Head of Cloud Engineering
NorthStar Labs

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Johnson <maya.johnson@northstarlabs.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: NorthStar launch — Dedicated capacity sizing
Attachments: capacity_workbook_NSL_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), autoscale_policy_draft.md (text)

Maya — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise ops-first proposal to get you started; attached is a workbook with our modeled rps-to-GPU mapping and a draft autoscale policy you can mark up. Summary recommendations (high level):

1) Baseline Reserved Pool:
- Baseline slab: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs dedicated (steady-state sizing to cover 120 rps at p95 latency target), with a safety buffer of +20% for routine variance.

2) Burst Pool + Policy:
- Burst capacity: flexible pool up to 24x A100-equivalent GPUs available for short windows (this is a soft pool shared across our Dedicated customers in the region with priority routing).
- Pre-approved burst window: up to 12 hours/day for the first 72 hours post-launch; microburst allowance of up to 30 minutes at 8x for sudden surges.
- Credit model: first 8 hours of burst usage during the launch window are billed at committed rate (counts toward monthly commitment); additional burst hours within the launch window are billed at overage rate unless pre-funded via burst credits.

3) Autoscale behaviour (ops guardrails):
- Prewarm: 5 minute prewarm for warmed model variants (e.g., same-architecture warm cache); cold-start prewarm for full model load ~120–180s depending on model weight (we recommend using warm cache priming before expected spikes).
- Scaling granularity: step-sizes of 2 GPUs; upscales allowed at sub-30s decision latency for traffic surges when KV cache ready.
- Eviction/fallback: graceful eviction policy with oldest non-active instances reclaimed first; automatic routing to lower-cost model variant (quantized 4-bit) after 10m sustained overload with explicit SLA decline notice.

4) SLAs and telemetry hooks:
- Operational SLO we propose: maintain p95 token-latency <= 150ms for the primary model under burst up to 4x; we commit to availability > 99.5% for reserved slab.
- Telemetry: token-level cost and latency hooks to your CloudOps team (we'll provide a streaming webhook + dashboard link).

5) Runbook & MAP:
- We included a mutual action plan in the workbook (tab 3). Short version: dry-run staging test 2 weeks before launch, 48-hour prewarm window to seed KV caches, and a control-room on launch day to exercise manual bump if needed.

Next steps:
- Rishi will follow up with the commercial mapping (credits, commitment tiers) and we can align an ops dry-run date. If you want, we can narrow the burst pool size down (e.g., 16x) to fit budget — the workbook has alternative scenarios.

Happy to hop on a 30m with CloudOps & Procurement this week to walk the workbook.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Maya — looping in Procurement on pricing mechanics. Quick commercial notes to accompany Lukas's ops proposal:

- Commitment tiers: the recommended baseline (8x + 20%) maps to our "Small Dedicated" tier. Burst pool access is sold as a combination of pre-funded burst credits (recommended: 48 hours pre-funded at overage rate) plus an on-demand overage rate.
- Crediting: for launch-specific events we can offer a one-time launch credit equal to 10% of the projected overage cost if you sign the SOW and MAP within 10 business days.
- DocuSign path: I'll generate an amendment that attaches the MAP as Exhibit A and quantifies the burst-credit commitment. Procurement, please confirm the required PO lead time and any internal approvers.

Proposed next steps: Rishi to share draft amendment (target: 2025-11-07), Lukas to schedule ops dry-run (target week of 2025-12-29).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: NorthStar launch — Dedicated capacity sizing (ops guardrails + acceptance criteria)

Maya — quick operational guardrails from the infra/ops side and a proposed acceptance checklist we use for launch events. Quoting Lukas below for context:

On Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 1:02 PM Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Maya — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise ops-first proposal to get you started; attached is a workbook with our modeled rps-to-GPU mapping and a draft autoscale policy you can mark up.

Key guardrails (runbook-friendly):
- Rolling preheat: 48-hour prewarm window recommended to prime KV caches across all critical endpoints; this mitigates the cold-start tail and reduces required burst headroom.
- Surge throttling: if sustained load > 6x baseline for > 30 minutes we trigger a staged throttle (inform + gradual token drop) and open a P1 incident; Redwood will provide an RTO estimate and run remediation playbook.
- Model fallback sequencing: 1) warm cache prime, 2) scale additional GPUs, 3) route to quantized variant (fallback); explicit telemetry alert at each step so NorthStar can automate client-side retry/backoff.

Acceptance checklist (short):
1) Dry-run pass in staging with simulated 5x sustained load for 2 hours.
2) Telemetry routing validated to CloudOps (webhook + dashboard).
3) MAP signed and DocuSign amendment executed.

We accept the MAP credit structure Rishi proposed; legal can finalize language in the amendment. If this looks good we'll lock the dry-run date during our next sync — available slots: 2025-12-15, 2025-12-29, or 2026-01-05.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
